alerts.headline: Flood Warning issued November 6 at 9:17AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
alerts.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Heavy rainfall will cause a continued rise through Moderate flood
stage through the end of the week at the St. Johns River near Cocoa.
The river is then forecast to rise into Major flood stage this
weekend and into early next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:15 AM EST Friday the stage was 16.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:15 AM EST Friday was 16.9 feet.
- Fore

alerts.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 6 at 1:25AM EST until November 8 at 2:00AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
alerts.areas: Coastal Volusia; Coastal Indian River; Coastal St. Lucie; Coastal Martin; Mainland Northern Brevard; Northern Brevard Barrier Islands; Mainland Southern Brevard; Southern Brevard Barrier Islands
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents expected.

* WHERE...The beaches of Volusia, Brevard, Indian River, Saint
Lucie and Martin counties.

* WHEN...Through late Saturday night.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.

advisories.text: Update to the St. Johns River flood warning near Cocoa in Brevard County: rain water is still draining into the river. The river near Cocoa is expected to crest at major flood stage on Friday, higher than the crest after Hurricane Ian, and to stay flooded to some degree for weeks. Do not drive around barricades or through flooded areas, and use caution near the riverbanks.

The flood warning for the St. Johns River near Cocoa in Brevard County is still in effect. At 7:15 PM Thursday the river stood at 16.9 feet, which is above the 16.0-foot flood stage and in moderate flood stage. NWS expects it to reach major flood stage late this week and stay there through the weekend and into early next week. Do not drive around barricades or through flooded roads near the river.

advisories.agency: National Weather Service Melbourne (as reported by Florida Today)
advisories.text: The St. Johns River near Cocoa is expected to reach major flood stage. The Providence Road area west of Cocoa could become impassable and cut off access to the Mullet Lane and Bass Road area. Water could also flood low-lying areas near the river, including Lake Poinsett west of Cocoa, the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park area of Cocoa. Do not drive through flooded roads near the river.

Update to the St. Johns River flood warning near Cocoa (9 miles west) in Brevard County: at 8:15 AM Friday the river stood at 16.9 feet, above the 16.0-foot flood stage, and moderate flooding is happening now. NWS now expects the river to keep rising, reach major flood stage this weekend and crest at about 17.1 feet late this weekend into early next week. The warning stays in effect until further notice. At 17.2 feet the Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes impassable, cutting off access to the Mullet Lane and Bass Road area. Do not drive around barricades or through flooded areas, and use caution near the riverbanks.
